title.en: Rama Banished: The Old Javanese Ramayana Opens in the Forest
title.zh: 羅摩流放：古爪哇《羅摩衍那》開篇於林中

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE; reliefs carved c. 9th century (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919), Prambanan and Panataran relief narrative; Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: The oldest surviving major work of Javanese literature retells Rama's story in courtly kakawin verse: exiled through his father's old promise, Rama leaves Ayodya with his wife Sinta and his brother Leksmana for the Dandaka forest, refusing royal comforts for the fourteen years of exile — the episode carved at the head of the Prambanan relief cycle.
summary.zh: 爪哇文學最古之偉構以典雅頌詩重述羅摩故事：因父王舊諾而遭放逐，羅摩攜妻悉多、弟勒什曼那入檀陀迦林，十四年放逐甘捨王宮之樂——此段即普蘭巴南浮雕長卷之首章。

sensitivity.note: Javanese Ramayana tradition (kakawin); a shared Hindu-Javanese heritage; passages are condensed paraphrases of the kakawin narrative as it is read in the relief commentary.

passages.text: Bound by the old promise made to a junior queen, King Dasa Rata of Ayodya must send his heir Rama into exile. Rama accepts without protest, and Sinta and his brother Leksmana insist on sharing the forest life; the three leave the palace, and the court of Ayodya follows them with laments.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin (c. 9th c.), opening cantos, as read in Kats' relief commentary (1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: In the Dandaka forest the exiles take up the ascetic life: Rama in bark garments, Sinta learning forest fare, Leksmana building their leaf-hut. The Kakawin dwells on the beauty of the forest exile as much as the hardship, for the poem was composed for a Javanese court that read the story as its own sacred genealogy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

title.en: The Golden Deer and the Abduction of Sinta

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin Marica episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: The demon Marica transforms into a golden deer that grazes before Sinta's hut; while Rama pursues it and Leksmana draws the protective circle, the rakshasa king Rawana approaches disguised as an old beggar, seizes Sinta, and carries her through the air toward Alengka as the mountain birds scatter.
summary.zh: 羅剎摩里遮化作金鹿，現於悉多茅舍之前；羅摩追鹿、勒什曼那畫護圈之際，十首魔王拉瓦那假扮老乞婆近前，一把抱起悉多，乘空而遁，群鳥驚散。

sensitivity.note: Kakawin paraphrase via the relief commentary; the abduction episode heads the Prambanan narrative frieze.

passages.text: A wondrous deer of gold appears grazing before the hermitage. Sinta, charmed, begs Rama to catch it; the deer is the demon Marica transformed, and as Rama's arrow finds it the dying demon imitates Rama's own voice crying for help.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, Marica episode (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: Believing his brother's cry, Leksmana leaves the protective circle he had drawn; in that instant Rawana approaches Sinta in the guise of an old ascetic, gains her confidence, then seizes her. As Rawana carries her skyward toward Alengka, the birds of the forest scatter before him and Sinta drops her ornaments for anyone who may follow.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

title.en: Jatayu Falls: The Old Eagle Who Fought the Ten-Faced King

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin Jatayu episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: The great eagle Jatayu, old friend of Rama's house, attacks Rawana in mid-air to stop the abduction; his wings are cut, and he falls dying to the rocks, his claws still fixed in the demon king. Rama later finds him, and from the dying eagle learns for the first time where his wife has been carried.
summary.zh: 巨鷹賈塔尤——羅摩家門之故交——凌空攔截拉瓦那；其翼被斬，抱著魔王墜岩而死。羅摩後至，自垂死神鳥之口始知愛妻去向。

sensitivity.note: Kakawin paraphrase via relief commentary; bird-hero motif.

passages.text: Hearing Sinta's cries, the ancient eagle Jatayu rises against Rawana's flying chariot and grapples with the ten-faced king in the sky, tearing at his chariot and armor; but Rawana severs his wings with his sword, and the old bird falls dying on the mountain rocks.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, Jatayu episode (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: Rama and Leksmana, searching, find the broken Jatayu and hear from him the tale of the abduction — that Sinta lives and is carried to Alengka. The eagle dies in Rama's arms, and the brothers perform his funeral rites before turning toward the south in grief.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

title.en: Subali and Sugriwa: The Monkey Brothers' Feud
title.zh: 蘇巴利與蘇格里瓦：猴族兄弟之爭

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin Subali-Sugriwa episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: In the Kakawin's telling, the monkey-king Subali has seized his brother Sugriwa's throne and wife; Rama's arrow pierces Subali as the brothers duel, and the dying Subali rebukes Rama for killing from hiding. Sugriwa is restored and pledges his monkey host to the search for Sinta.
summary.zh: 猴王蘇巴利奪弟蘇格里瓦之王位與妻室；兄弟相搏之際，羅摩一箭穿蘇巴利之身。垂死猴王責羅摩藏於暗處殺人。蘇格里瓦復位，傾其猴兵以助羅摩尋妻。

sensitivity.note: Kakawin paraphrase via relief commentary; note the moral ambiguity of Rama's arrow, which the Javanese poem sharpens.

passages.text: The mighty Subali, invulnerable to his enemies, has driven his brother Sugriwa from the throne of the monkeys and taken his wife. Sugriwa, hunted through the forest, meets Rama and pledges his service if Rama will slay his brother.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, Subali episode (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: As the two monkey-brothers close in battle, indistinguishable in their fury, Rama from cover pierces Subali with an arrow. The dying Subali confronts Rama: is it hero's work, to kill unseen the mightiest of monkeys? Rama answers that justice against the wrong done to a brother is the law of kings; Sugriwa is enthroned and gathers his host for Rama.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

title.en: Hanuman's Embassy: The Tail Set Alight in Rawana's Court

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin Hanuman embassy episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: Sent across the sea as Rama's envoy, Hanuman finds Sinta in the Asoka garden and delivers his message; seized and brought before Rawana, he mocks the ten-faced king to his face. Ordered to be burned, he wraps his tail in oil-soaked cloth — and with the burning tail leaps free, setting the golden city of Alengka itself on fire.
summary.zh: 哈奴曼奉羅摩之命渡海為使，於如意林中覓見悉多、傳遞口信；被擒押至拉瓦那殿前，仍当面譏誚十首王。王命焚其尾——他以油布裹尾；尾一著火，他便掙脫而起，反將金色之城阿楞迦付之一炬。

sensitivity.note: Kakawin paraphrase via relief commentary; the burning of Alengka is among the most carved Prambanan panels.

passages.text: Hanuman leaps the ocean and, shrinking to monkey size, searches the Asoka garden until he finds Sinta under guard; kneeling, he gives her Rama's token and message and carries back her answer. Provoked by the rakshasa women, he is seized and dragged before Rawana's throne.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, Hanuman embassy (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: Before the ten-faced king the monkey-envoy will not kneel; Rawana orders his tail wrapped in cloth and set on fire. Hanuman slips his bonds, leaps free trailing flame, and runs the ramparts and gates of Alengka, leaving the golden city burning behind him before returning over the sea.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin leap episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: Chosen for the reconnaissance across the water, Hanuman grows to the size of a mountain, pauses on the mount of spring (Mahendra) to gather himself, and takes the leap: over fish and sea-demons who rise to test him, over the island-city of the rakshasas — the Kakawin lingers on his flight as the poem's showpiece of heroic transformation.
summary.zh: 哈奴曼受選渡海偵察，身長如山；立於摩亨陀山巔蓄勢一躍——海中魚怪躍起相試，被他一一越過；直抵羅剎島城。爪哇頌詩以此飛躍為英雄變身之絕筆。

passages.text: The monkeys seek one able to cross the sea unaided, and Hanuman is chosen: he grows vast as a mountain and takes his stand on the mount of spring, then leaps — the sky fills with his passage and the sea rises in waves beneath him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, leap episode (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: Mid-ocean, sea-demons and fish rise to seize the flying monkey by his shadow; he mocks them, dips a paw, and passes on until the towers of Alengka rise on the horizon and he lands, small again, among the rakshasa city's trees.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

title.en: Trijata's Dream: Sinta Comforted in the Asoka Garden
title.zh: 特里賈塔之夢：如意林中的慰藉

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin Trijata episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: Held in the Asoka garden, Sinta refuses Rawana's suit under threat of death; the rakshasa princess Trijata — who has dreamed Alengka burning and Rawana dragged by monkeys — takes Sinta's side, warns the garden's guards, and comforts her: the omen says the ten-faced king's power is already breaking.
summary.zh: 悉多被囚如意林，拒拉瓦那之求而遭死脅；羅剎公主特里賈塔夜夢阿楞迦烈火焚城、十首王為群猴所曳——遂站到悉多一邊，告誡園中看守，並慰其心：異兆已示十首王氣數將盡。

sensitivity.note: Kakawin paraphrase via relief commentary; the female ally within the enemy city.

passages.text: In the garden of Asoka trees Sinta, guarded by rakshasa women, refuses Rawana's suit even under the threat of the sword. The rakshasa princess Trijata, Rawana's kin but his conscience, has seen in dream the city burning and the ten-faced king dragged headlong by monkeys.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, Trijata episode (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: She tells Sinta the dream and gives her protection against the garden's tormentors; Sinta, half despondent, half comforted, waits in the garden — the omen has named the outcome of the war before the monkey host has crossed the sea.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

title.en: Wibhisana Defects: The Righteous Brother of the Ten-Faced King
title.zh: 維比薩那來歸：十首王之義弟

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin Wibhisana episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: Rawana's younger brother Wibhisana, alone at court, counsels returning Sinta and saving Alengka; Rawana denounces him before the assembly, and Wibhisana crosses to Rama's camp, where the monkeys suspect a spy until Rama accepts him as a brother — the Kakawin's figure of the divided family of the rakshasas.
summary.zh: 十首王之弟維比薩那於殿上力諫：還妻以救阿楞迦。拉瓦那當眾斥之；維比薩那遂投羅摩大營——群猴疑其為細作，羅摩以兄弟相待，納之。爪哇詩中，羅剎王族之裂由此始。

passages.text: When the war-omen darkens, Wibhisana stands in Rawana's council as the single voice for surrendering Sinta; Rawana publicly reviles him as a traitor before the rakshasa chiefs, and Wibhisana departs over the water to the monkeys' camp.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, Wibhisana episode (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: Sugriwa's counselors cry spy, but Rama receives the rakshasa prince, takes his counsel, and accepts him as a brother — the Kakawin lets the defection stand as proof that righteousness, not race, is the measure of kinship in the war for Sinta.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

title.en: Kumbakarna Roused: The Sleeper Who Fights His Own King's War
title.zh: 醒來的昆巴卡那：為君而戰的沉睡者

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin Kumbakarna episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: When Alengka's armies break, the giants rouse Kumbakarna, the vast brother who sleeps half the year. He first rails at Rawana for bringing ruin on the house by stealing another's wife — then, because he is Rawana's brother, takes up his club for the doomed city and dies fighting the monkeys, ground at last by Rama's arrows.
summary.zh: 阿楞迦軍潰之際，羅剎們喚醒半年沉睡之巨靈昆巴卡那。他先痛斥拉瓦那：劫他人之妻而傾家國！——然身為其弟，終提杵為將亡之城而戰，力戰群猴，卒亡於羅摩箭雨之下。

sensitivity.note: Kakawin paraphrase via relief commentary; the Javanese Kumbakarna is more moralizing than his Indian counterpart, a favourite of wayang.

passages.text: The sleeping giant Kumbakarna must be roused with drums and slaughter as his appetite wakes; told of the war he rebukes Rawana to his face — the abduction of Sinta, he says, will destroy the rakshasa house — yet when the king calls on his loyalty as a brother, the giant takes up his club for Alengka.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, Kumbakarna episode (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: He crashes through the monkey host, devouring and dashing, until Rama's arrows find him; the giant falls denouncing the war he could not refuse. The Kakawin grants him the dignity of the man who tells the truth and then dies for the kinship he is bound by.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

title.en: The Bridge of Stone Across the Sea

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin bridge episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: The monkey host builds the causeway to Alengka: monkeys, bears and spirits hurl boulders into the strait until a bridge of stone runs across the sea, and Rama's army pours over it — the Kakawin and the Prambanan sculptors alike relish the spectacle of an army of monkeys as engineers.
summary.zh: 猴兵築堤跨海：猿、熊、神魔向海峽擲石，石橋乃成；羅摩大軍踏橋而渡。爪哇頌詩與普蘭巴南石刻同樣沉迷於群猴為工程師之奇觀。

passages.text: On the advice of the sea, the army resolves to bridge the strait: monkeys tear up mountains, bears carry boulders, and the stones, thrown into the water, bind together into a causeway that runs to the walls of Alengka.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, bridge episode (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: Rama's host crosses the stone bridge in column, the sea churning under the weight of the monkeys, and the rakshasa sentries bring the news to Rawana that the son of Dasa Rata has brought the forest itself against the city.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕群）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, c. 9th century CE (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); kakawin final battle

texts.license: Public domain (1919); kakawin story content public domain

summary.en: At the last, Rama and Rawana meet on the field: each arrow cut off is answered by a new head or new arms, until Rama's great arrow flies at the one mortal spot. The ten-faced king of Alengka falls, the city mourns its king, and Wibhisana is installed in his place — the kakawin closes its war with the funeral of a magnificent enemy.
summary.zh: 決戰之場，羅摩對拉瓦那：斬一首則生一首，斬一臂則生一臂；直至羅摩神箭射中那唯一之致命處。十首王殞命，滿城舉哀；維比薩那受立為王——爪哇頌詩以一位壯麗敵人之葬禮收束全詩之戰。

passages.text: In the last duel every head and arm Rawana loses grows again, and the battle seems endless; Rama, instructed by the gods' favour and Wibhisana's word, draws the great arrow and aims not at the heads but at the mortal centre of the ten-faced king.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, final battle (Kats 1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: Rawana falls, and even the monkeys stand silent at the fall of so great an enemy. Wibhisana performs the funeral and is enthroned in Alengka; Rama, Sinta restored, prepares the return toward Ayodya.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Old Javanese Ramayana kakawin, as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

region.en: Prambanan, Central Java (relief cycle and later Javanese wayang versions)
region.zh: 中爪哇普蘭巴南（浮雕及爪哇哇揚戲後世版本）

texts.period: Old Javanese Ramayana tradition and Javanese wayang retellings (Kats 1919)

source.work: J. Kats, Het Ramayana op Javaansche tempel reliefs (1919); Javanese Ramayana tradition, fire-ordeal episode

texts.license: Public domain (1919); story content public domain

summary.en: Rescued but publicly doubted, Sinta ascends the pyre herself and calls on Agni to speak her truth: the fire does not burn her, and the god rises with her in his arms to declare her pure. The Javanese tradition gives the ordeal to Sinta's own initiative — the trial that proves her is one she demands.
summary.zh: 悉多雖獲救而遭眾疑，遂自登火堆，呼火神阿耆尼為證：烈焰不傷其身，火神抱之而出，向眾宣告其貞潔。爪哇傳統中，此歷火之判乃悉多自請——證明她的考驗，由她自己發起。

sensitivity.note: Fire-ordeal episode; flagged interpretive on gender — the Javanese versions vary in how the ordeal is framed.

passages.text: Doubt falls on Sinta's year in captivity, and rather than endure it she commands the pyre to be built: ascending the flames herself she calls on Agni, god of fire, as witness of her truth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Javanese Ramayana tradition (fire ordeal), as read in Kats (1919); not verbatim.

passages.text: The pyre burns and leaves her untouched; Agni rises bearing her and proclaims to the host that fire has found nothing to consume. The Kakawin and the wayang alike close the episode on the public vindication of Sinta before the monkey host and the rakshasa captives.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Javanese Ramayana tradition; not verbatim.
